arxiv-2104-04856.creator: Edvard P.G. Bruun, Rafael Pastrana, Vittorio Paris, Alessandro Beghini, Attilio Pizzigoni, Stefana Parascho, Sigrid Adriaenssens
arxiv-2104-04856.description: Abstract Geometrically complex masonry structures (e.g., arches, domes, vaults) are traditionally built with expensive scaffolding or falsework to provide stability during construction. The process of building such structures can potentially be improved through the use of multiple robots working together in a cooperative assembly framework.

arxiv-2106-12440.title: Influences of Dielectric Constant and Scan Rate on Hysteresis Effect in Perovskite Solar Cell with Simulation and Experimental Analyses
arxiv-2106-12440.creator: Jun-Yu Huang, You-Wei Yang, Wei-Hsuan Hsu, En-Wen Chang, Mei-Hsin Chen, Yuh-Renn Wu
arxiv-2106-12440.description: Abstract In this work, perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with different transport layers were fabricated to understand the hysteresis phenomenon under a series of scan rates. The experimental results show that hysteresis phenomenon would be affected by the dielectric constant of transport layers and scan rate significantly.

arxiv-2107-02084.title: Artificial SA-I and RA-I Afferents for Tactile Sensing of Ridges and Gratings
arxiv-2107-02084.description: Abstract For robot touch to reach the capabilities of human touch, artificial tactile sensors may require transduction principles like those of natural tactile afferents. Here we propose that a biomimetic tactile sensor (the TacTip) could provide suitable artificial analogues of the tactile skin dynamics, afferent responses and population encoding.

arxiv-2304-11485.title: Understanding Lexical Biases when Identifying Gang-related Social Media Communications
arxiv-2304-11485.creator: Dhiraj Murthy, Constantine Caramanis, Koustav Rudra
arxiv-2304-11485.description: Abstract Individuals involved in gang-related activity use mainstream social media including Facebook and Twitter to express taunts and threats as well as grief and memorializing. However, identifying the impact of gang-related activity in order to serve community member needs through social media sources has a unique set of challenges.

arxiv-2305-00499.title: Numerical tests of the large charge expansion
arxiv-2305-00499.creator: Gabriel Cuomo, J. M. Viana Parente Lopes, José Matos, Júlio Oliveira, and João Penedones
arxiv-2305-00499.description: Abstract We perform Monte-Carlo measurements of two and three-point functions of charged operators in the critical O ⁡ ( 2 ) O(2) model in 3 dimensions. Our results are compatible with the predictions of the large charge superfluid effective field theory.

pmc-10546993.title: Mesenteric Arterial Thrombosis Revealing Relapse of Nephrotic Syndrome in Young Women
pmc-10546993.creator: Maryem Ferjani, Yosra Zaimi, Nouha Trad, Yousra Hammi, Myriam Ayari, Shema Ayadi, Taha Sayari, Tahar Gargah
pmc-10546993.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundNephrotic syndrome (NS) is associated with a hypercoagulable state and may be complicated by thrombotic events. Venous thrombosis is well-acknowledged, while arterial thrombosis is rather unusual.Case PresentationWe present the case of a 20-year-old woman with a 12-year history of idiopathic NS revealed by extensive cerebral venous thrombosis with pulmonary embolism treated with anticoagulation therapy and oral corticosteroid therapy followed by mycophenolate mofetil (MMF). The thrombophilia assessment did not show any abnormalities.

pmc-10780957.title: Hydralazine-Induced Vasculitis: Case Insights and Literature Review for Informed Clinical Recognition and Management
pmc-10780957.creator: Divya Shah
pmc-10780957.description: Hydralazine, a commonly prescribed medication for hypertension, has been associated, albeit rarely, with the development of vasculitis. The case presentation involves a 51-year-old female with diabetes and hypertension who presented with a distinctive rash, pancytopenia, and positive findings for various antibodies. A collaborative approach involving rheumatology, hematology, and dermatology was crucial in diagnosing leukocytoclastic vasculitis attributed to hydralazine.

pmc-11433111.title: Significant Differences in Microbial Soil Properties, Stoichiometry and Tree Growth Occurred within 15 Years after Afforestation on Different Parent Material
pmc-11433111.creator: Emre Babur
pmc-11433111.description: The mineralogical composition of the parent material, together with plant species and soil microorganisms, constitutes the foundational components of an ecosystem’s energy cycle. Afforestation in arid-semi arid regions plays a crucial role in preventing erosion and enhancing soil quality, offering significant economic and ecological benefits.

pmc-11482652.title: Diagnosis and management of early pregnancy loss
pmc-11482652.creator: Vrati M. Mehra, Salwa Farooqi, Pallavi Sriram, Modupe Tunde-Byass
pmc-11482652.description: elvic ultrasonography, preferably transvaginal, to investigate pregnancy viability and distinguish early pregnancy loss from an ectopic pregnancy. Diagnosis of early pregnancy loss requires determination of serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels and pelvic ultrasonography, preferably transvaginal, to investigate pregnancy viability and distinguish early pregnancy loss from an ectopic pregnancy. Treatment options include expectant, medical, and surgical management.

pmc-11581636.title: Medication Changes Among Older Drivers Involved in Motor Vehicle Crashes
pmc-11581636.creator: Andrew R. Zullo, Melissa R. Riester, Adam M. D’Amico, Monika Reddy Bhuma, Marzan A. Khan, Allison E. Curry, Melissa R. Pfeiffer, Seth A. Margolis, Brian R. Ott, Thomas Bayer, Nina R. Joyce
pmc-11581636.description: IMPORTANCEAlthough older adults may use potentially driver-impairing (PDI) medications that can produce psychomotor impairment, little is known about changes to PDI medication use among older adults from the time before to the time after a motor vehicle crash (MVC).OBJECTIVETo quantify use of and changes in PDI medications among older adults before and after an MVC.

pmc-11996089.title: Social Determinants of Health Associated with Cholangiocarcinoma Risk in High-Risk Areas of Thailand: A Case-Control Study
pmc-11996089.creator: Pranom Khuanthong, Nopparat Songserm, Comsun Thongchai, Wilawun Chada
pmc-11996089.description: Objective: This case-control study sought to explore the social determinants of health (SDH) associated with cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) risk in high-incidence regions of Thailand. Methods:The research was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 assessed the prevalence, context, and conditions among at-risk populations for CCA in Yasothon, located in Northeast Thailand.

pmc-12584485.title: Assessing the knowledge, attitudes and practices towards malaria prevention and determinants of antenatal care utilization among pregnant women in Sekyere South district, Ghana; a cross-sectional study
pmc-12584485.creator: Clement Naayaara Zuuri, Dominic Kofi Gyamah, Loviah Buabeng, Ruth Mensah
pmc-12584485.description: BackgroundMalaria in pregnancy contributes significantly to poor maternal health outcomes, accounting for 17.6% of outpatient visits in Ghana. The Ashanti Region, particularly Sekyere South District, bears a high burden despite interventions, such as ITN distribution and intensified IPTp education. Limited evidence exists on how pregnant women’s knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) influence preventive behaviours and ANC use in this setting.

pmc-12619907.title: Advancing toxicity AI-based prediction with multilevel systems biology: a case study on genotoxicity
pmc-12619907.creator: Xin Zhang, Huazhou Zhang, Xiao Yun, Wenxiao Pan, Qiao Xue, Xian Liu, Jianjie Fu, Aiqian Zhang
pmc-12619907.description: The rapid expansion of chemical diversity presents substantial challenges for health and environmental risk assessment, necessitating the development of alternative, high-throughput computational methodologies. A key hurdle in toxicity prediction lies in the heterogeneous nature of adverse health outcomes at the tissue and cellular levels, as biological processes exhibit cell-type-specific and context-dependent responses.

pmc-12711900.title: Current protected areas provide limited benefits for European river biodiversity
pmc-12711900.creator: James S Sinclair, Rachel Stubbington, Ellen A R Welti, Jukka Aroviita, Nathan J Baker, Miguel Cañedo-Argüelles, Zoltán Csabai, David Cunillera-Montcusí, Sami Domisch, Martial Ferréol, Mathieu Floury, Marie Anne Eurie Forio, Peter L M Goethals, Alexia M González-Ferreras, Kaisa-Leena Huttunen, Richar
pmc-12711900.description: Protected areas are a principal conservation tool for addressing biodiversity loss. Such protection is especially needed in freshwaters, given their greater biodiversity losses compared to terrestrial and marine ecosystems. However, broad-scale evaluations of protected area effectiveness for freshwater biodiversity are lacking.

pmc-12990358.title: A systematic comparison of methodologies for the estimation of the serial interval
pmc-12990358.creator: Lanlan Yu, Yunyi Cai, Gui-Quan Sun, Jiancheng Lv, Quan-Hui Liu
pmc-12990358.description: Serial interval (SI) is a crucial indicator for characterizing the course of epidemic transmission and provides guidance in designing the intervention strategy for preventing epidemic spreading. Many approaches have been developed to estimate the serial intervals, while their effectiveness evaluations are rarely exhibited due to the unavailable of the real SI values.

pmc-13049981.title: Primordial odontogenic tumor: a case report of a rare entity in the Saudi population
pmc-13049981.creator: Asma Almazyad, Nasser Almadan, Ahad Bin Juwaid, Abeer Alfadhel, Marwa Almarwan, Abdulsalam Aljabab
pmc-13049981.description: IntroductionPrimordial odontogenic tumor (POT) is a rare, benign, mixed epithelial–mesenchymal neoplasm, histologically characterized by spindle- to stellate-shaped cells in a fibromyxoid stroma resembling dental papilla, bordered by columnar epithelium. It occurs mainly in children and adolescents, often in the posterior mandible, and radiographically presents as a well-defined radiolucency associated with unerupted teeth.

pmc-13398995.title: Microdosimetry in BNCT
pmc-13398995.creator: Gustavo A Santa Cruz
pmc-13398995.description: ed or calculated microdosimetric spectra are almost invariably linked to variations in the radiobiological properties of radiation fields. In boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT), the complexity of the radiation field extends beyond the conventional description of a mixed neutron–photon primary field. A fundamental challenge arises from the small number of secondary high‐LET particles required to deliver therapeutic doses.

pmc-13511518.title: Seizure-Related Deterioration in Treated Glioma: A Narrative Review of Nonconvulsive Status Epilepticus, Peri-Ictal Pseudoprogression, Treatment-Related Change, and True Progression
pmc-13511518.creator: Polina Chliapnikov, Mark Bernstein
pmc-13511518.description: Background/Objectives: In glioma patients, acute neurologic deterioration may reflect nonconvulsive status epilepticus (NCSE), peri-ictal pseudoprogression, treatment-related change, or true progression. As these entities share imaging features, misdiagnosis can delay therapy. This review synthesizes evidence relevant to a proposed electroclinical-imaging framework for distinguishing seizure-related deterioration from treatment-related change and true progression.
